newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt Airport forecasts substantial 96 profits.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt Airport forecasts substantial 96 profits.

text.p: Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG), owner and manager of Frankfurt airport, said it expected a "substantial" rise in net profits this year.
FAG chairman Wilhelm Bender said the company had budgeted for a 43 million marks profit in 1996 after achieving a post-tax profit of 44.2 million marks last year.
But he told a news conference: "This year we will substantially improve on those profits.
"Although we have not had strong (traffic) growth this year, we have achieved a major financial result," he added.
FAG forecast a turnover of 2.4 billion marks in 1996 compared to 2.3 billion marks in 1995, he added.
Passenger numbers looked set to just fall short of 40 million compared to 38 million last year, Bender said.
Air cargo volumes would end in the 1.3-1.4 million tonnes range after totalling 1.33 million tonnes in 1995.
FAG said its supervisory board had approved internal re-structuring aimed at further improving company efficiency.
The seven new business units, reflecting airport processes, would operate as profit centres and would have to sell any internal services at market prices, Bender said.
He would be responsible for the passenger and external operational business units, and his deputy Manfred Schoelch would run freight logistics and ground handling services.
The remaining units would be managed by board members Johannes Endler and Hans Georg Michel.
FAG supervisory board chairman and Hesse finance minister Karl Starzacher said the state of Hesse had no plans to sell its 45 percent stake in FAG.
This might appear to be a short-term solution to financial problems but the state wanted to continue to influence operations at Frankfurt airport, he added.
He welcomed Bonn's decision not to sell its 26 percent holding in FAG and said the city of Frankfurt did not plan to sell its 29 percent holding either.
